verse.text: Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.

reflection.scripture: Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
reflection.observation: Isaiah 60 is a song of restoration for Jerusalem — a promise that God's light will shine so brightly that even nations and kings are drawn to it. This isn't about Israel's own brilliance; it's about the radiance of God's presence reflected through them. The image is magnetic and inviting — light that doesn't force but attracts, dawn that signals a new day after long darkness.
reflection.application: Where is God calling me to be light in a dark place? It might not be a grand stage — maybe it's showing patience in a tense conversation, offering hope to a discouraged friend, or simply living with joy that makes others curious. My 'brightness' isn't self-generated; it's a reflection of time spent with God. Today, I'll look for one small way to let His light shine through me.
reflection.prayer: Father, You are the source of all light. Shine through me today — not for my glory, but so others might be drawn to You. Help me reflect Your love, peace, and hope in every interaction. Let my life be a small glimpse of Your dawn. Amen.
